question: Does Workday (NASDAQ: WDAY) report a gross or net retention metric in its annual or quarterly reporting? If so, provide the definition
answer:
Workday tracks and reports on Gross Revenue Retention Rate. 

The company defines Gross Revenue Retention Rate as the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers and is calculated by taking total annual recurring revenue (“ARR”) of our customers as of the corresponding prior period-end and comparing that to ARR from that same set of customers as of the current period-end. The metric takes into account recurring revenues lost to product or customer churn but does not account for additional revenue earned from add-ons or net expansions, which include volume and price adjustments.

model_answer:
## Short answer

**Gross — yes. Net — no (not anymore).** Workday discloses a **gross revenue retention rate** (a revenue/ARR-based retention metric) with a stated definition and an approximate figure in the MD&A ("Gross Revenue Retention Rate" section) of its Form 10-K and Form 10-Q. It **no longer discloses a net revenue retention rate**; it dropped that metric in late 2024 and now substitutes a quantification of subscription revenue growth from existing vs. new customers.

## The gross revenue retention rate definition (current, verbatim from the FY2026 10-K and Q2 FY2027 10-Q)

> "Our growth in subscription services revenues attributable to existing customers is further reflected by our gross revenue retention rate of approximately **97%** as of January 31, 2026 [and approximately **97%** as of July 31, 2026 in the Q2 FY2027 10-Q]. Our gross revenue retention rate measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers and is calculated by taking total annual recurring revenue ("ARR") of our customers as of the corresponding prior period-end and comparing that to ARR from that same set of customers as of the current period-end. The metric takes into account recurring revenues lost to product or customer churn but does not account for additional revenue earned from add-ons or net expansions, which include volume and price adjustments. Our high gross revenue retention rate demonstrates our ability to maintain our existing customer base and drive strong overall customer satisfaction.
>
> Our gross revenue retention rate is based on ARR, which represents the annualized value of active subscription contracts as of the end of each period. Each subscription contract is annualized by dividing the total contract value by the number of days in the contract term and then multiplying by 365. We exclude certain subscription contracts from the calculation, including contracts with terms less than one year that are distinct from our core product offering, such as contracts for tenants which are used for implementation and testing. To the extent that we are negotiating a renewal with a customer after the expiration of the subscription, ARR is only adjusted if the customer churns. We calculate ARR on a constant currency basis using exchange rates set at the beginning of each fiscal year."

(The FY2025 10-K used the same language with "approximately **98%** as of January 31, 2025" and added the sentence "ARR is a non-GAAP financial measure and should be viewed independently of, and not as a substitute for or combined with, revenue and unearned revenue.")

Key features: it is **ARR-dollar-based** (not logo-based), measured on a **same-customer cohort** basis (prior period-end ARR of the customer set vs. current period-end ARR for that same set), **excludes expansion/add-ons and price/volume uplifts**, captures only churn/down-sell, is computed at **constant currency**, and is disclosed only as a rounded ("approximately") figure.

## What happened to the net retention metric

- **Through the Q2 FY2025 10-Q (period ended July 31, 2024)**, Workday disclosed only qualitative/floor statements: gross and net revenue retention "exceeded 95% and 100%," respectively, with a definition that defined net retention as: *"the net change in recurring revenue from existing customers… includes both positive and negative impacts on revenue, such as add-ons, net expansions, and product and customer churn… calculated by taking the current period-end ARR of our customers that we retained year-over-year, including add-ons and net expansion, divided by the total ARR at the end of the corresponding prior period."*
- **SEC comment letters (Aug./Sept. 2024)** asked Workday to define the metrics, state whether they are KPIs, quantify them historically, and ensure they reflected current trends. In its **September 19, 2024** response letter, Workday said it "**no longer intends to include disclosure related to net revenue retention rates** in our SEC filings" — calling NRR "largely duplicative of the change in revenue from existing customers" — while it would **continue to disclose the gross revenue retention rate**, and would disclose "the actual, then-current gross revenue retention rate for each period in future filings."
- Consistent with that, since the **FY2025 10-K** (filed March 11, 2025) each 10-K/10-Q contains the quantified gross revenue retention rate and definition above, and replaces NRR with a mix-of-growth disclosure (e.g., FY2026: "approximately 60% of the increase in subscription services revenues was attributable to expansion within our customers that existed as of the beginning of the comparable prior year period, and the remaining 40% was attributable to customers added after…").
- A full-text search of EDGAR for "net revenue retention" in Workday's filings returns only the two 2024 comment letters and the Q2 FY2025 10-Q — confirming no net retention metric in any filing since then.

## Reported values

| Disclosure | Period | Gross revenue retention |
|---|---|---|
| 10-K (FY2026) | Jan 31, 2026 | ~97% |
| 10-K (FY2025) | Jan 31, 2025 | ~98% |
| Q2 FY2027 10-Q | Jul 31, 2026 | ~97% |

Caveats worth noting: the figure is presented as **"approximately"** (rounded, not a precise KPI), management has said it does **not** consider retention rates to be key performance indicators used to run the business (they are "supplemental data"), and the company has said it will only give more precision/context if changes are material.

Sources: Workday FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 3/6/2026) and FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 3/11/2025), Item 7; Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q (period ended 7/31/2026), Item 2; Workday CORRESP letters dated 9/4/2024 and 9/19/2024 (SEC, CIK 0001327811).
